# SPD-054 — Bash hook: a trap string runs a command the hook never reads (Law 7)

## Brief
trap stores shell code the shell runs later (EXIT, DEBUG before every command, ERR, signals), and analyse_words dispatches trap as kind other, so a member's git write inside a trap string is silent.

Evidence: Probed from the SPD-043 scratchpad with a fake git first on PATH (zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2, sh): trap 'git push' EXIT ran git push in all four; the hook on main reads kind other with no finding. SPD-043 only treats trap as leaving every variable uncertain. The harness itself refuses shell text naming trap in a worktree session, which is no cover for the hook in other sessions.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children: one hook fix in bin/spud_ledger.py (a trap branch in analyse_words beside eval and a shell's -c string, and trap in GLOB_COMMAND_SAMPLES) with red-first tests in tests/test_hooks.py, the same shape as SPD-043 and SPD-046, built in worktree spd-054-trap-string. Design settled by Spud at start: the action string is read as shell text the way eval's words and a shell's -c string are, with its own quotes, at a working directory the hook treats as unknown since the string runs later; a string the hook cannot resolve is refused for a member; the list, print and reset forms stay silent; Spud is unchanged.
